messages.author: Affairs and Order
messages.text: <@307290318590705667> that's a fair point, a war shouldn't be decided while one side is asleep. The War Board proposal in #announcements (vote closes Friday 16:00 UTC) is built around this (1 turn = 1 real hour, nobody can rush or stall), but it won't be in the game for a while. So what should we do in the meantime? Do you all want wars to last longer now (e.g. a minimum of a day, or a cap on how much a side can lose per hour while offline), or just wait for the new system? Drop your ideas here. I'll put the best options into the weekly vote.

messages.author: Dede

messages.author: Andrew
messages.text:
Other option is to start the war at less points (maybe 1/3, or 1/4), and increase time for each turn. DnS wars typically took 2-3 days at the least, and because each action type had a cap of 12 points, and you only regenerated 1 per 2 hours, you could "bank" 24 hours of action, so you wouldn't cap yourself if someone attacked just as you went to bed, and it also took longer for wars to be won, allowing for more of a fair chance. 

Tbh, I wouldn't even mind a war starting at 0 action points, or maybe tie in the action points at start to different war types, maybe something like a Blitzkrieg lets you start with both sides having half of cap, but in exchange your side has a debuff which gets worse over time to simulate stretched and underprepared supply lines etc.
